subject: economics
title: Demand, Supply and Equilibrium
welcome_lead: Where the two curves cross - the heart of microeconomics.
meta_desc: A-Level Microeconomics: demand, supply and market equilibrium.
final_note: Equilibrium is where buyers and sellers agree on price and quantity.

concepts.def: Quantity buyers want at each price, ceteris paribus.
Quantity sellers offer at each price, ceteris paribus.
Price where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

Other things being equal - a key assumption.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lower price means more affordable units and substitution from other goods, so quantity demanded rises. Supply typically slopes up - higher price covers higher marginal cost and rewards extra output.
If price is above equilibrium, surpluses pile up and force price down. If price is below equilibrium, queues form and price rises. The market gropes toward equilibrium.
A change in price causes a movement along the curve. A change in income, tastes, costs or technology shifts the whole curve, giving a new equilibrium.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
A change in price shifts the demand curve.
Demand always falls when supply increases.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
Demand always falls when supply increases.

mcqs.q: What causes the supply curve to shift?
options: Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
Changes in production costs, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of producers, expectations — anything affecting supply other than the good's own price.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
